model.name: Project
model.purpose: Represent a bounded unique undertaking that is authorized to pursue stated goals with allocated resources, a beginning and an intended end, and a governed path from initiation through delivery, control, close and evaluation.
model.scope_statement: The project as the undertaking itself: identity and classification; authorization and continued justification; goals, scope, benefits and constraints; governance roles and decision rights; work breakdown and interfaces; resource allocations and performance baselines; progress, change, risk, issue and assurance; lifecycle states and events including abort, suspend, merge, restart and continuing-operations variants; closeout, transition, disposal and post-project evaluation; and stewardship of the project record. Delivery approach may be predictive, incremental, iterative, adaptive, hybrid or agile. The model is format-neutral: JSON, YAML, documents, Git, MCP or document stores are projections.
in_scope: Identity and classification of the undertaking
Progress, change, risk, issue and assurance
Lifecycle states and events including abort, suspend, merge, restart and continuing-operations variants
Closeout, transition, disposal and post-project evaluation
Delivery approach as predictive, incremental, iterative, adaptive, hybrid or agile
Format-neutral projections: JSON, YAML, documents, Git, MCP or document stores
out_of_scope: Programmes and portfolios as containers or strategic investments that initiate and direct one or more projects (sibling WM-ACT-029 / ISO 21503 / ISO 21504 / NASA program definition).
The plan or schedule as the intention or time-phased model of work (sibling plan-and-schedule model); this model binds to a plan, it does not own the schedule semantics.
Repeatable process or workflow definitions (sibling process model); a project may use processes but is not itself a repeatable process.
Atomic performed acts or actions (sibling act model); work packages resolve to acts, they are not stored as the project.
Task as the assignable work unit (contained sibling WM-ACT-006); the project holds breakdown and allocation, not the task execution record.
Milestone and deliverable as first-class delivery objects (contained sibling WM-ACT-031); the project links to them and tracks gate results, it does not redefine their schemas.
Person, organization, asset and location master records.
Enterprise financial ledgers, commercial contracts and product configuration baselines except as references from allocations, commitments and deliverable links.
Competency frameworks for practitioners (ISO/WD 21515) and AI-application concepts (ISO/DIS 21520), which are adjacent standards not yet in this object's schema.

boundary_notes.distinction: A project is temporary and unique; a process is continuous and repeatable. Ongoing product-mode work is a project only when an authorized bounded undertaking is declared.
A project is the undertaking; a plan is the intended steps. W3C PROV treats Plan as an entity used by agents in activities; do not collapse project, plan and activity.
A project is contained by a programme or portfolio when one exists, but a standalone project remains valid. ISO 21502 explicitly does not guide programme or portfolio management.

NASA distinguishes a project (specific investment with requirements, life-cycle cost, beginning and end) from a programme (strategic investment that initiates and directs projects), including the single-project-programme special case.
Work-package versus task: ISO 21511 WBS elements are the project-side decomposition; WM-ACT-006 holds assignable task records. Dual modelling of the same leaf work is a conflict to avoid.
Benefits may be owned by a programme or sponsoring organization while the project contributes outcomes; ISO 21502 still expects benefits practices inside the project lifecycle.
Do not claim conformance to ISO 21502, PMBOK, PRINCE2 or GovS 002 from alignment alone.

sources.title: ISO 21502:2020 Project, programme and portfolio management — Guidance on project management
sources.relevance: Normative project-management guidance; applicable to any organization and any project regardless of purpose, delivery approach, lifecycle model, complexity, size, cost or duration. Explicitly excludes programme and portfolio management. Delivery approaches include predictive, incremental, iterative, adaptive or hybrid, including agile.

sources.title: ISO 21500:2021 Project, programme and portfolio management — Context and concepts
sources.relevance: Foundational context for project, programme and portfolio management and for adopting the ISO/TC 258 series. Points to ISO 21502, 21503, 21504 and 21505 for further guidance.

sources.title: ISO 21511:2018 Work breakdown structures for project and programme management
sources.relevance: Guidance on WBS terms, definitions, concepts, characteristics, uses, integration and relationships with other breakdown structures. Does not prescribe tools. Annexes give examples and related structures.

sources.title: Improving project management
sources.relevance: First-party ISO overview of the 21500 series: 21502 practices across the lifecycle including planning and control, risk, issues, change control, benefits, business and societal change and information; also 21503, 21504, 21505 governance, 21508 earned value, 21511 WBS.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Activity, Entity, Agent, Plan, Association, startedAtTime, endedAtTime, wasAssociatedWith, wasGeneratedBy, wasAttributedTo, atLocation. Alignment only; a project is not identical to prov:Activity or prov:Plan.

sources.title: NPR 7120.5F NASA Space Flight Program and Project Management Requirements, Chapter 2
sources.relevance: Mandatory NASA space-flight project definition, categorization, Formulation/Implementation lifecycle, KDPs, LCRs, FAD, Formulation Agreement, Project Plan, Decision Authority, Management Agreement, Agency Baseline Commitment, WBS, EVM above cost threshold, Decision Memorandum, continuing-operations initial-capability cost, decommissioning.

sources.title: Government Functional Standard GovS 002: Project Delivery
sources.organization: Government Project Delivery and Cabinet Office, United Kingdom
sources.relevance: Mandated UK government expectations for portfolios, programmes and projects. Eight elements: about the standard; principles; overview and context; governance and roles; portfolio management; programme and project management; planning and control; solution delivery. v2.1 adds policy and evaluation context, senior officer accountable for project delivery, mandatory governance roles, and transition, use and disposal of a solution; references The Teal Book and the Senior Responsible Owner.

sources.title: What is a Project, Examples and the Project Lifecycle
sources.relevance: Official PMI definition: a project is a temporary endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result. Describes a project lifecycle of phases culminating in deliverables, including feasibility, design and build. Direct HTTP fetch was blocked; wording is taken from the live PMI page as returned by search of that URL.

sources.title: PRINCE2 Project Management Practitioner (Version 7)
sources.relevance: Seven principles, seven practices addressed continuously through the lifecycle, seven processes from initiation to delivery, defined roles, people management, sustainability and ESG, digital and data management, and mandatory tailoring to project context.

sources.title: ISO 21505:2017 Project, programme and portfolio management — Guidance on governance
sources.relevance: Governance context for projects, programmes and portfolios; intended for governing bodies, sponsors, steering committees, portfolio owners and the project management office; also usable for assessment, assurance or verification of the governance function.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: Establish which undertaking this is, how it is named and typed, and which delivery and risk class applies, without treating storage keys as meaning.
bundles.rationale: Groups the Identifiers and Typology and delivery approach layers so that identity and class are recorded without treating storage keys as meaning.

layers.name: Identifiers
layers.description: Hold master, global and local identifiers and human-readable names for the project record.

findings.name: Project record identity
findings.description: A project is a distinct authorized undertaking and must be uniquely identifiable in the sponsoring organization's master register. NASA requires an official listing of programs and projects in the OCFO Meta-Data Manager, with the project category recorded in the Formulation Authorization Document and Project Plan. PMI treats the project as a named temporary endeavor. W3C PROV identifies activities and entities by IRI. Dates, status values and version timestamps are not identifiers. Alternate names, codes and IRIs may exist but the master-system identifier is authoritative.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this project and which register issued it?
If the master identifier is absent or not shareable, what governed IRI or Dimension-assigned UUID/ULID uniquely names this project?
answer_data: dimension_uid (ulid-or-uuid, required when master id is absent)

questions.text: What display name and alternate names are in current use, and which name is canonical for sponsor reporting?
When was this identity first observed or ingested, and which agent attributed the register entry?

data_elements.name: project_master_id
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier assigned by the sponsoring organization's project register or equivalent master system.

data_elements.name: issuing_system
data_elements.description: Name or IRI of the master register that minted project_master_id.

data_elements.name: global_iri
data_elements.description: Optional governed global identifier or IRI for cross-system exchange.

data_elements.name: dimension_uid
data_elements.description: UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master or global identifier exists.

data_elements.name: display_name
data_elements.description: Human-readable project name as used in charters and reports.

data_elements.name: alternate_names
data_elements.description: Codes, short names, contract names or partner names that must not replace the master identifier.

artifacts.name: Project register entry
artifacts.description: Master-system listing of the project, including official identifier, name and issuing organization, analogous to NASA's Meta-Data Manager listing.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by project_master_id as minted by the issuing register; the register record URL is an alternate locator.

layers.name: Typology and delivery approach
layers.description: Classify the undertaking by type, category, sector, delivery approach and location of performance without encoding a single methodology as mandatory.

findings.name: Classification and delivery approach
findings.description: ISO 21502 applies regardless of delivery approach and lists predictive, incremental, iterative, adaptive and hybrid including agile. NASA categorizes projects 1, 2 or 3 from life-cycle cost, radioactive material, human space flight and priority, with Center assignment as performing location. PMI phases such as feasibility, design and build are a lifecycle framing, not a universal taxonomy. Classification must record what kind of project this is and how it will be delivered, while remaining silent on file format. Sector-specific classes (space flight, major government project, construction, research) are alignments, not a single closed enum claimed as globally complete.

questions.text: What category, sector and delivery approach apply, and which standard or policy table produced that class?
Where is the project assigned to perform, including multi-site or international partner locations?
Which classification-driven constraints apply, such as mandatory EVM, independent review, or human-spaceflight extra controls?
How does this local class map to ISO 21502 delivery-approach language and to any partner taxonomy?

data_elements.name: project_category
data_elements.description: Sponsoring-system category or class, such as NASA Category 1/2/3 or UK major/departmental/mega project class.

data_elements.name: delivery_approach
data_elements.description: predictive, incremental, iterative, adaptive, hybrid, agile, or a named local method.

data_elements.name: sector_or_domain
data_elements.description: Application domain such as space flight, public infrastructure, digital, research.

data_elements.name: performing_location_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to performing organization site, NASA Center, or multi-site set.

data_elements.name: priority_level
data_elements.description: Sponsor priority used in categorization or portfolio ranking, not a substitute identifier.

artifacts.name: Classification section of FAD or Project Plan
artifacts.description: Documented category, delivery approach and performing organization as required in NASA FAD/Project Plan and as expected in GovS 002 governance context.
media_or_form: section of the Formulation Authorization Document or Project Plan
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent FAD or Project Plan document identifier plus section reference, under project_master_id.

bundles.name: Intent and authorization
bundles.description: Record why the undertaking exists, who authorized it, what success looks like, and where scope starts and stops.
bundles.rationale: Groups the Authorization and justification and Goals, scope and benefits layers so the instrument that creates the project, its continuing justification and its bounded objectives are recorded together.

layers.name: Authorization and justification
layers.description: Capture the instrument that creates the project and the continuing business justification that keeps it alive.

findings.name: Charter and continued justification
findings.description: A project does not exist as an authorized use of resources until a sponsoring authority issues a charter-equivalent instrument. NASA uses a project Formulation Authorization Document to authorize a project manager to plan, then a Formulation Agreement and Project Plan; Implementation proceeds only after a Decision Authority KDP. PMI describes the project as a temporary endeavor whose existence is framed by the lifecycle. PRINCE2 Version 7 retains continued business justification as a principle and uses processes from starting up and initiating through closing. UK GovS 002 treats governance and roles, including the Senior Responsible Owner, as mandatory direction. Withdrawal of justification is a first-class close or abort path, not a missing field.

questions.text: Which authority issued the charter-equivalent instrument, and what resource-application powers did it grant the project manager?
When did authorization take effect, and when was that fact observed or ingested into this record?
Is continued business justification still valid, threatened or withdrawn, and what evidence supports that status?
Who may read the authorizing instrument, and which partner or classified portions are excepted?

data_elements.name: authorization_instrument_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of the charter, FAD, PID or equivalent authorizing document.

data_elements.name: authorizing_authority_ref
data_elements.description: Person or body that authorized existence and resource application.

data_elements.name: authorized_at
data_elements.description: Event time when authorization became effective.

data_elements.name: justification_statement
data_elements.description: Current business or mission justification, including why the project should continue.

data_elements.name: justification_status
data_elements.description: valid, threatened, withdrawn, or under-review.

data_elements.name: project_manager_authority_scope
data_elements.description: Authority granted to apply organizational resources to project activities.

artifacts.name: Project charter, FAD or equivalent authorization
artifacts.description: Instrument that formally authorizes the project and the project manager's authority to apply resources. NASA FAD; PMI charter concept; PRINCE2 initiation products.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by authorization_instrument_id assigned by the sponsoring authority, bound to project_master_id.

layers.name: Goals, scope and benefits
layers.description: State objectives, success criteria, in-scope and excluded work, intended benefits and outcome owners.

findings.name: Goals, scope, benefits and boundaries
findings.description: ISO 21502 focuses on benefits and outcomes from inception to completion and treats planning and control, benefits, business and societal change and information as lifecycle practices. PMI frames the project as creating a unique product, service or result through phases that complete deliverables. NASA Project Plans state objectives, requirements, technical and management approach and commitments. GovS 002 v2.1 explicitly includes policy and evaluation context. Scope must record inclusions, exclusions, assumptions and constraints so the undertaking is bounded. Benefits may later be owned by operations or a programme; the project still records the intended contribution and measures used to judge success.

questions.text: What objectives and quantified success criteria is this project pursuing, and who owns each measure?
What is in scope, what is excluded, and which assumptions or constraints bound the undertaking?
Which intended benefits does the project contribute, and does a programme, sponsor or operations owner hold realization after handover?
Which parent programme, policy objective or strategic goal does this project's purpose serve?

data_elements.name: objective_set
data_elements.description: Each objective with statement, measure, target, priority and success criterion.

data_elements.name: scope_inclusions
data_elements.description: Work, products or results that are in scope.

data_elements.name: scope_exclusions
data_elements.description: Explicit out-of-scope items to prevent silent expansion.

data_elements.name: assumptions_and_constraints
data_elements.description: Assumptions, constraints, dependencies and imposed dates or funding limits.

data_elements.name: intended_benefits
data_elements.description: Expected advantages or value, measures, owners and realization window.

data_elements.name: success_criteria
data_elements.description: Acceptable evidence that the undertaking achieved its purpose.

artifacts.name: Scope, objectives and benefits statement
artifacts.description: Charter, Project Plan or equivalent section stating objectives, scope boundaries, success criteria and intended benefits.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent charter or Project Plan identifier plus section reference, bound to project_master_id.

bundles.name: Governance and accountability
bundles.description: Name who directs the project, who decides, who assures, and how the method is tailored and verified.
bundles.rationale: Groups the Decision rights and roles and Tailoring and compliance layers so direction, decision rights and the method actually in force are recorded together.

layers.name: Decision rights and roles
layers.description: Bind sponsor, senior responsible owner, decision authority, project manager, boards and resource owners.

findings.name: Decision rights and roles
findings.description: ISO 21505 addresses governing bodies, sponsors, steering committees and those who direct projects. ISO 21502 includes project governance and project organization and roles as core concepts. NASA requires a Decision Authority who determines whether and how the project proceeds, a governing PMC, a project manager accountable for safety, technical integrity, cost, schedule and mission success, and Center oversight. GovS 002 v2.1 makes portfolio, programme and project governance roles mandatory, adds a senior officer accountable for project delivery in the organization, and points to the Senior Responsible Owner. PRINCE2 Version 7 teaches defined roles and responsibilities plus people management. Role occupancy is time-bounded and may transfer; the role is not the person master record.

questions.text: Who is the senior accountable owner of this project, and on whose behalf does the project manager act?
Who is the Decision Authority or equivalent, what may they decide, and what is reserved to a higher board or legislature?
When did each current role assignment start, and is there a planned end or transfer?
Which person and organization records do these roles reference, including multi-Center or partner contributors?

data_elements.name: sponsor_or_sro_ref
data_elements.description: Accountable senior owner (sponsor, SRO or equivalent).

data_elements.name: decision_authority_ref
data_elements.description: Body or individual who authorizes phase progression and commitments.

data_elements.name: project_manager_ref
data_elements.description: Person accountable for directing the undertaking within the management agreement.

data_elements.name: governing_board_ref
data_elements.description: Project board, PMC, steering committee or equivalent.

data_elements.name: assurance_roles
data_elements.description: Independent or internal assurance, technical authority, standing review board.

data_elements.name: role_assignments
data_elements.description: Role, agent reference, authority limits, start and end times.

artifacts.name: Governance and organization section of the Project Plan
artifacts.description: Named Decision Authority, governing board, sponsor/SRO, project manager and assurance roles with accountabilities.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent Project Plan identifier plus governance section reference, bound to project_master_id.

layers.name: Tailoring and compliance
layers.description: Record the method actually in force, what was tailored, and how compliance is evidenced.

findings.name: Tailoring and compliance
findings.description: ISO 21502 is guidance, not a certified management system, and is delivery-approach-neutral. PRINCE2 Version 7 requires the method to be tailored to the project's size, context and complexity. NASA requires a Compliance Matrix attached to the Formulation Agreement or Project Plan, allows tailoring with permission of the requirement owner, and records deviations and waivers. GovS 002 is mandated for UK departments and arm's length bodies but is designed to apply to all types of government projects. Alignment with a named method is evidence, not proof of conformance. Competing method stacks (PMI process groups, PRINCE2 processes, NASA phases A–F, ISO lifecycle practices) must be recorded as the adopted profile, not merged into a false universal process.

questions.text: Which method profile is actually in force, and is any conformance claimed with evidence?
Who approved each tailoring or waiver, and what expiry or conditions apply?
Where is the live compliance matrix, and which requirements remain unmet?
How does the adopted profile map to partner methods when more than one organization is directing work?

data_elements.name: adopted_method_profile
data_elements.description: Named methods in force, such as ISO 21502 practices, PRINCE2 7, NASA NPR 7120.5, GovS 002, local hybrid.

data_elements.name: tailoring_decisions
data_elements.description: Requirement or practice tailored, rationale, approver, evidence.

data_elements.name: compliance_matrix_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to the live compliance or tailoring matrix.

data_elements.name: conformance_claim
data_elements.description: none, aligned, or evidenced-conformant, never implied.

data_elements.name: waiver_set
data_elements.description: Waivers or deviations with owner, expiry and conditions.

artifacts.name: Compliance or tailoring matrix
artifacts.description: NASA-style Compliance Matrix or equivalent mapping of required practices to adopted, tailored or waived status.
media_or_form: matrix attached to the Formulation Agreement or Project Plan
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by compliance_matrix_ref pointing at the live matrix for project_master_id.

bundles.name: Structure and resources
bundles.description: Describe how work is decomposed, how nested tasks and deliverables attach, and what people, money and assets are committed.
bundles.rationale: Groups the Work breakdown, Nested work and interfaces and Allocations and baselines layers so decomposition, nested links and committed resources stay together without absorbing sibling models.

layers.name: Work breakdown
layers.description: Hold the project-side decomposition of scope into controlled elements.

findings.name: Work breakdown structure
findings.description: ISO 21511 provides WBS terms, concepts, characteristics, uses and relationships to other breakdown structures for project and programme management, without prescribing tools. NASA requires a product-based WBS used to organize phase work, documented in the Project Plan, with additional structure in the NASA WBS Handbook; EVM setup begins as soon as WBS, Organizational Breakdown Structure and Integrated Master Schedule exist. The WBS is the project's framework for managing work, not the task execution log and not the milestone or deliverable object model. Related structures (OBS, product breakdown, cost breakdown) are linked, not duplicated. ISO/DIS 21511 is in development; current implementations should record which WBS edition they follow.

questions.text: What identifier and edition define the controlling WBS, and which element is the root for this project?
Which WBS elements decompose this project, and which of them are control accounts versus planning packages?
Which OBS, product breakdown or cost breakdown is integrated with this WBS?
What evidence shows the WBS covers the entire authorized scope and is configuration-controlled?

data_elements.name: wbs_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of the controlling work breakdown structure.

data_elements.name: wbs_edition
data_elements.description: ISO 21511:2018, NASA handbook, local, or mixed.

data_elements.name: wbs_elements
data_elements.description: Element id, parent, name, type, scope statement, control account flag.

data_elements.name: obs_ref
data_elements.description: Organizational breakdown used with the WBS.

data_elements.name: related_breakdown_refs
data_elements.description: Product, cost or other breakdowns related per ISO 21511 Annex B.

artifacts.name: Work breakdown structure and dictionary
artifacts.description: Hierarchical decomposition of project scope with element definitions, control accounts and links to related breakdowns.
media_or_form: hierarchical work breakdown structure with dictionary entries
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by wbs_id and wbs_edition, with element ids resolved under the project root element.

layers.name: Nested work and interfaces
layers.description: Link the project to tasks, milestones, deliverables, other projects and external interfaces without absorbing those siblings.

findings.name: Nested work, deliverables and interfaces
findings.description: Registry composition says a project contains tasks (WM-ACT-006) and contains milestones and deliverables (WM-ACT-031). NASA projects may interface to other projects, agencies and international partners, and programmes initiate and direct projects. ISO 21511 relates the WBS to other structures rather than treating every product or milestone as a WBS-only concept. Leaf work must not be duplicated as both a WBS element and a task with conflicting identity. Interfaces, including reimbursable and partner work, are typed relationships with direction and effectivity, not parent-child dumping.

questions.text: Which tasks, milestones and deliverables does this project contain or bind, and at which WBS elements?
Which programme or portfolio contains this project, and which peer projects or partner organizations does it interface with?
Which repeatable processes or workflows does this unique undertaking use without becoming those processes?
When did each nested or interface link become effective, and when was it withdrawn?

data_elements.name: contained_task_refs
data_elements.description: References to WM-ACT-006 task records, usually at or below work-package level.

data_elements.name: milestone_refs
data_elements.description: References to WM-ACT-031 milestone records this project is measured against.

data_elements.name: deliverable_refs
data_elements.description: References to WM-ACT-031 deliverable records the project is to produce.

data_elements.name: parent_programme_ref
data_elements.description: Containing programme or portfolio (WM-ACT-029) when one exists.

data_elements.name: peer_project_interfaces
data_elements.description: Typed interfaces to other projects, agencies or partners with direction and effectivity.

data_elements.name: process_refs
data_elements.description: Repeatable processes used inside this unique undertaking.

artifacts.name: Interface and composition index
artifacts.description: Index of contained tasks, milestone and deliverable links, parent programme and peer interfaces, with effectivity.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by project_master_id plus link_id for each nested or interface entry, with effective_from and effective_to.

layers.name: Allocations and baselines
layers.description: Record committed people, funds and assets and the cost, schedule and content baselines those commitments support.

findings.name: Resource allocations and performance baselines
findings.description: A project is resourced by allocations of people, money and assets for stated periods. NASA documents time-phased cost plans, a Management Agreement that defines the manager's control parameters, Unallocated Future Expenses, and an Agency Baseline Commitment at KDP C against which Implementation performance is measured; continuing-operations projects with unspecified Phase E end establish an initial capability cost instead of a full life-cycle end. ISO 21508 in the 21500 series addresses earned value against a performance measurement baseline. GovS 002 planning and control practices include resource and baseline control. Allocations are owned by the resource-providing party even while the project record references them. Changing a baseline is not an informal edit; it is a change-controlled event.

questions.text: What people, funds and assets are currently allocated, to which WBS elements, and for which periods?
Which resource-owning party committed each allocation, and what happens if they withdraw it?
What identifiers and as-of times distinguish the current cost, schedule and content baselines, including ABC or initial capability cost?
When did each allocation start and end in event time, and when was the change ingested?

data_elements.name: allocations
data_elements.description: Resource reference, type (person, team, funds, asset), quantity, unit, WBS element, period start/end, owning party.

data_elements.name: cost_baseline
data_elements.description: Baselined cost plan, currency, as-of time, ABC or equivalent.

data_elements.name: schedule_baseline_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to the plan-and-schedule model's baselined integrated master schedule.

data_elements.name: content_baseline_ref
data_elements.description: Baselined scope or technical content committed at the last gate.

data_elements.name: management_agreement
data_elements.description: Control parameters and authorities currently granted to the project manager.

data_elements.name: unallocated_reserve
data_elements.description: UFE or analogous reserve, holding level and access rules.

artifacts.name: Baseline and allocation pack
artifacts.description: Current Management Agreement or equivalent, cost and content baselines, and the allocation register for people, funds and assets.
media_or_form: Management Agreement, baseline records and allocation register
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by baseline identifiers with as-of times under project_master_id; superseded baseline versions retain their own version identity.

bundles.name: Control, assurance and uncertainty
bundles.description: Show how the undertaking is measured, changed, threatened and independently assessed while it is live.
bundles.rationale: Groups the Progress measurement, Change control, Risk, issue and exception and Reviews, gates and assurance layers so a live undertaking is measured, changed, threatened and independently assessed under one responsibility.

layers.name: Progress measurement
layers.description: Hold status, forecasts and earned-value or alternative progress measures.

findings.name: Progress and earned value
findings.description: ISO 21502 treats planning and control as lifecycle practices. The ISO series includes ISO 21508 earned value management; NASA mandates EVM and EIA-748 for projects above the stated life-cycle cost threshold, with performance-measurement-baseline reporting from Phase B, and treats EVM as optional below the threshold except where contracts require it. EVM is not universal: non-developmental work, steady-state operations and basic research are called out by NASA as not requiring EVMS. Alternative measures (milestone burn, agile throughput, benefit leading indicators) must be named when EVM is not used. Status reports are periodic accounts, not the project itself. Forecasts are distinct from baselines.

questions.text: Which progress method is in force, and what are the current earned-value or alternative measures as of the last period?
What cost and finish forecasts exist, and how do they diverge from the current baseline?
What reporting cadence, audience and product are agreed with the sponsor or oversight body?
When were measures observed versus when the underlying work event occurred, and what is the quality or surveillance status of the measurement system?

data_elements.name: status
data_elements.description: Current managerial status such as formulating, executing, paused, breached, closing.

data_elements.name: progress_method
data_elements.description: evm, milestone-weighted, agile-throughput, hybrid, qualitative.

data_elements.name: evm_measures
data_elements.description: PV, EV, AC, SPI, CPI, EAC, VAC and as-of time when EVM applies.

data_elements.name: forecast
data_elements.description: Estimate at completion, finish date forecast, confidence or JCL where required.

data_elements.name: period_accomplishments
data_elements.description: Narrative accomplishments for the reporting period.

data_elements.name: reporting_cadence
data_elements.description: Agreed cadence and audience for progress reporting.

artifacts.name: Status report or IPMR-equivalent
artifacts.description: Periodic progress account including accomplishments, measures, forecast and concerns; NASA IPMR where EVM contracts apply.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by project_master_id plus reporting period at the agreed cadence; NASA IPMR identifiers apply where EVM contracts require them.

layers.name: Change control
layers.description: Control changes to baselines, requirements, allocations and configuration of the undertaking.

findings.name: Integrated change control
findings.description: ISO 21502 names change control among planning and control practices. NASA requires significant divergence from the Management Agreement to be accompanied by an amended Decision Memorandum, and treats Integrated Baseline Reviews as required when EVM applies and for major changes that significantly impact cost and schedule. Uncontrolled baseline edits destroy the meaning of progress. Change requests have identity, impact assessment, decision, effectivity and provenance. Configuration of WBS, requirements and product baselines may sit in sibling configuration models; the project records the change decision that binds them.

questions.text: Which change requests are open against this project, and which baselines would they alter?
Who decided each approved change, and was that within the Management Agreement or did it require a higher Decision Memorandum amendment?
When did the change event occur, when did it become effective, and when was it ingested?
Which changes are forbidden without sponsor or statutory approval, including external commitments and launch dates?

data_elements.name: change_request_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of a proposed or approved change.

data_elements.name: change_class
data_elements.description: baseline, requirement, allocation, technical, documentary.

data_elements.name: impact_assessment
data_elements.description: Cost, schedule, content, risk and benefit impacts.

data_elements.name: decision
data_elements.description: approved, rejected, deferred, superseded.

data_elements.name: decision_authority_for_change
data_elements.description: Who was empowered to accept this class of change.

data_elements.name: effectivity_at
data_elements.description: When the approved change became effective.

artifacts.name: Change log and decision record
artifacts.description: Register of change requests with impact assessments, decisions and baseline amendments, including Decision Memorandum amendments.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by project_master_id; entries keyed by change_request_id with effectivity_at.

layers.name: Risk, issue and exception
layers.description: Log threats, opportunities, realized issues and manage-by-exception breaches.

findings.name: Risk, issue and exception
findings.description: ISO 21502 includes addressing risks and issues in planning and control. PRINCE2 Version 7 treats risk, issues and progress as continuous practices and retains manage-by-exception as a principle. NASA evaluates adequacy of the risk management approach at life-cycle reviews and requires top technical, cost, schedule and safety risks with mitigations in baselines. A risk is an uncertain event; an issue is a realized problem; an exception is a breach of delegated tolerance. Opportunities are in-scope where the adopted method tracks them. Likelihood and impact scores are method-specific and must name the scale. Handling may escalate to the programme or enterprise risk register without deleting the project-level record.

questions.text: What are the current top risks by residual impact, which milestones or WBS elements they threaten, and who owns the response?
Which issues are open, which are closed, and which changes or exceptions did they trigger?
What tolerances are in force, which exceptions have been raised, and who was they escalated to?
Who raised each risk or issue, when did the identification event occur, and when was it ingested?

data_elements.name: risk_items
data_elements.description: Description, cause, likelihood, impact, proximity, owner, response, residual, linked milestones or WBS.

data_elements.name: issue_items
data_elements.description: Realized problems, severity, owner, resolution, linked changes.

data_elements.name: opportunity_items
data_elements.description: Optional opportunities with owner and exploitation plan.

data_elements.name: tolerances
data_elements.description: Time, cost, scope, risk and benefit tolerances for manage-by-exception.

data_elements.name: exception_events
data_elements.description: Breaches of tolerance with escalation target and decision.

artifacts.name: Risk, issue and exception register
artifacts.description: Project-level register of uncertain threats and opportunities, realized issues, tolerances and exception escalations.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by project_master_id; entries keyed by risk, issue or exception item identifiers, retained when escalated to a programme or enterprise register.

layers.name: Reviews, gates and assurance
layers.description: Record independent and internal assessments that authorize or refuse progression.

findings.name: Reviews, gates and assurance
findings.description: NASA requires life-cycle reviews with six assessment criteria and Key Decision Points at which the Decision Authority determines readiness to proceed and records a Decision Memorandum; Standing Review Boards conduct specified LCRs with conflict-of-interest controls. ISO 21505 can be used for assessment, assurance or verification of the governance function. GovS 002 covers governance, roles and, through associated SRO guidance, senior accountability; v2.1 makes governance roles mandatory. PRINCE2 manages by stages and by exception, with stage-boundary and directing processes. A gate result is evidence, not a status label on the project identity. Failed or recycled gates, including NASA re-entry to Formulation for upgrades, are first-class events.

questions.text: What was the last gate or KDP result, including conditions, and which phase did it authorize?
Which Decision Authority and governing board signed the last Decision Memorandum, and who dissented?
What independent assurance was performed, against which criteria, and which findings remain open?
When was the review held, when was the decision signed, and when was that decision ingested?

data_elements.name: gate_or_kdp_id
data_elements.description: Identifier of the gate, KDP or stage boundary instance.

data_elements.name: review_type
data_elements.description: SRR, PDR, CDR, ORR, stage-boundary, PIR, special review, or local equivalent.

data_elements.name: expected_maturity
data_elements.description: Stated expected maturity state for this gate.

data_elements.name: result
data_elements.description: proceed, proceed-with-actions, recycle, stop, defer.

data_elements.name: decision_memorandum_id
data_elements.description: Record of the signed decision and conditions.

data_elements.name: assurance_findings
data_elements.description: Independent findings, severity and closure status.

artifacts.name: Gate or KDP decision pack
artifacts.description: Review materials, independent findings, Decision Memorandum or stage-boundary decision and conditions to proceed.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by gate_or_kdp_id with review_type and decision_memorandum_id under project_master_id.

bundles.name: Lifecycle and closure
bundles.description: Track the project's states and events from conception through close, abort, transfer, disposal and evaluation.
bundles.rationale: Groups the States and events and Closeout, disposal and evaluation layers so phases, rare transitions and closure remain one continuous record.

layers.name: States and events
layers.description: Model lifecycle phases, status and rare transitions without treating phase names as a single global enum.

findings.name: Lifecycle states and events
findings.description: ISO 21502 provides practices needed in each phase of the project lifecycle from inception to completion, remaining delivery-approach-neutral. NASA defines Formulation and Implementation with lettered KDPs, phases A–F, and special cases: two-step Announcement of Opportunity entry at KDP B, re-entry to Formulation for upgrades, continuing operations with unspecified Phase E end using initial capability cost, and decommissioning reviews. PRINCE2 processes run from starting up and initiating through controlling stages, managing product delivery, stage boundaries and closing. PMI describes a lifecycle of phases that culminate in deliverables. Status values such as initiated, executing, suspended, aborted, merged, transferred, closed-completed, closed-cancelled are operating states, not identifiers. Event time (chartered, paused, resumed, merged, aborted) is distinct from ingestion time.

questions.text: Which lifecycle model, phase and operating status apply right now, including suspended, aborted, merged or continuing-operations cases?
What are the planned and actual start and end (or initial-capability horizon), recorded as RFC 3339 event times with offset, and when were those facts ingested?
Has this project been split, merged, suspended, restarted, transferred to a new sponsor, or recycled to an earlier phase, and under which decision?
How do local phases map to partner lifecycle names when more than one authority is tracking the same undertaking?

data_elements.name: lifecycle_model
data_elements.description: Named lifecycle actually used: NASA A–F, PRINCE2 stages, ISO 21502 phases, PMI phases, hybrid.

data_elements.name: current_phase
data_elements.description: Current phase or stage in that model.

data_elements.name: current_status
data_elements.description: initiated, executing, suspended, aborted, merged, transferred, closed-completed, closed-cancelled, operations-continuing.

data_elements.name: planned_start
data_elements.description: Planned start event time with offset.

data_elements.name: planned_end
data_elements.description: Planned end or, for unspecified-end operations, the initial-capability horizon.

data_elements.name: actual_start
data_elements.description: Actual start event time.

data_elements.name: lifecycle_events
data_elements.description: Typed events: chartered, phase-entered, suspended, resumed, split, merged, aborted, transferred, closed.

artifacts.name: Lifecycle event log
artifacts.description: Append-only log of phase entries, suspensions, restarts, merges, aborts and closes with event time and Decision Authority reference.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by project_master_id; entries keyed by lifecycle event type and event time with a Decision Authority reference.

layers.name: Closeout, disposal and evaluation
layers.description: Complete, cancel, hand over, dispose and evaluate without losing the record.

findings.name: Closeout, disposal and evaluation
findings.description: PRINCE2 includes closing a project as a process. NASA includes decommissioning review to evaluate readiness for closeout, final delivery of remaining deliverables and safe disposal of assets, and requires archival of mission and science data. GovS 002 version 2.1 added clauses covering the transition, use and disposal of a solution, and added evaluation context. ISO/TC 258 has published ISO 21513:2026 guidance on post-project and post-programme evaluation; that text was not retrieved here and is an emerging alignment, not an implemented finding. Close may be completed, cancelled, merged or abandoned; warranty or liability tails may outlive operational close. Disposal and benefits handover can belong partly to operations or a programme; the project still records residual obligations.

questions.text: How was this project closed or why is it not yet closeable, including cancelled, merged or abandoned dispositions?
What was handed over to operations or another owner, and what disposal or decommissioning actions remain?
Which warranty, archive, classified-material or liability obligations survive close, and until when?
Where is the post-project evaluation, which questions did it answer, and is ISO 21513 used only as alignment?

data_elements.name: close_disposition
data_elements.description: completed, cancelled, merged, abandoned, transferred.

data_elements.name: handover_records
data_elements.description: What was handed to operations, a programme or another project, with acceptance.

data_elements.name: disposal_actions
data_elements.description: Asset or solution disposal, decommissioning and residual hazard actions.

data_elements.name: residual_obligations
data_elements.description: Warranty, liability, data-archive or classified-material obligations after close.

data_elements.name: evaluation_ref
data_elements.description: Post-project evaluation or lessons product reference.

data_elements.name: closed_at
data_elements.description: Event time of close decision or completion.

artifacts.name: Closeout, handover and evaluation report
artifacts.description: Disposition, accepted deliverables, residual obligations, disposal actions and post-project evaluation or lessons.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by project_master_id plus close_disposition and closed_at, with a reference to the post-project evaluation product.

bundles.name: Stewardship and exchange
bundles.description: Govern provenance, ownership, access, retention, deletion and interchange of the project record.
bundles.rationale: Groups the Provenance, ownership and access and Retention, deletion and interchange layers so the project record is governed from attribution through deletion and exchange.

layers.name: Provenance, ownership and access
layers.description: Attribute who produced and may see which parts of the project record.

findings.name: Provenance, ownership and access
findings.description: W3C PROV-O attributes entities to agents, associates agents with activities, records plans used, and timestamps starts and ends. NASA Decision Memoranda are signed by parties accepting supporting responsibilities. GovS 002 and the SRO role concentrate accountability in a senior owner; contributing parties still own their allocation data. Default access is owner-controlled need-to-know at bundle, layer, finding and artifact scope. Exceptions include statutory audit, classified compartments, partner-shared subsets and lawful whistleblowing. The sponsoring organization owns the project record; that is not the same as the project manager's Management Agreement. Software agents that ingest status must be recorded as prov:SoftwareAgent equivalents.

questions.text: Which organization owns the project record, and which contributing parties own their allocation or partner slices?
Which agents, including software ingest agents, are attributed or associated with the current charter, baseline and latest status, and which plan did they follow?
Who may read or mutate which bundle, layer, finding or artifact, and which classified or partner exceptions apply?
Where is the audit log of baseline edits, gate decisions and charter reads, and is it immutable?

data_elements.name: record_owner_ref
data_elements.description: Sponsoring organization that owns the project record.

data_elements.name: attribution_set
data_elements.description: PROV-style attribution of artifacts and findings to agents, including software ingest agents.

data_elements.name: access_class
data_elements.description: unclassified, official, confidential, secret, or local equivalent.

data_elements.name: access_grants
data_elements.description: Principal, scope (bundle/layer/finding/artifact), permission, expiry.

data_elements.name: audit_log_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to immutable access and mutation audit.

artifacts.name: Ownership, access and audit binding
artifacts.description: Named record owner, classification, grants and the audit trail for reads and mutations of charter, baseline and gate artifacts.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by project_master_id plus record_owner_ref and grant identifiers, with the audit_log_ref as evidence anchor.

layers.name: Retention, deletion and interchange
layers.description: Keep, redact, destroy and export project records without confusing projection format with semantics.

findings.name: Retention, deletion and interoperability
findings.description: NASA closeout includes archival of mission and science data and safe disposal of assets; the project record is not automatically deleted at operational close. GovS 002's transition, use and disposal clauses and public-sector records law (region-specific) drive retention. PROV bundles allow provenance of provenance for exchanged extracts. Interoperability is alignment to ISO 21500-series concepts, PMI vocabulary, PRINCE2 products, NASA templates and PROV activities, not a claim that a JSON document is the project. Deletion is a governed event with legal hold, redaction and tombstone behaviour. Format (JSON, YAML, XML, PDF, MCP, MongoDB) is a projection. A UK Teal Book programme-and-project data standard is reported in secondary UK guidance and is not treated as a retrieved normative schema here.

questions.text: Which retention schedule applies after close, and which legal holds currently block deletion?
If payload was deleted or redacted, who authorized it, what tombstone remains, and when did the event occur versus when it was ingested?
Which named exchange profile is used to import or export this project, and which concepts are declared aligned rather than conformant?
What projection currently serializes this record, and is any consumer treating that format as the meaning of the project?

data_elements.name: retention_schedule_ref
data_elements.description: Records schedule that governs the project file after close.

data_elements.name: legal_holds
data_elements.description: Holds that block deletion or alteration.

data_elements.name: deletion_or_redaction_events
data_elements.description: What was deleted or redacted, authority, event time, tombstone id.

data_elements.name: exchange_profile
data_elements.description: Named interchange profile: ISO-aligned, NASA templates, PRINCE2 products, PROV bundle, local.

data_elements.name: projection_type
data_elements.description: json, yaml, pdf, mcp, mongodb or other projection, never the semantics.

data_elements.name: tombstone_id
data_elements.description: Stable identifier retained after deletion of payload.

artifacts.name: Records schedule and exchange profile
artifacts.description: Binding of the project file to a retention schedule, legal-hold register, tombstone policy and named interchange profile.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by retention_schedule_ref bound to project_master_id; tombstone_id survives authorized deletion of payload.

functions.name: Authorize project
functions.description: Create the project record from a charter-equivalent instrument, bind sponsor and project manager authority, and set initial identity, category and justification.
inputs: Charter, FAD, PID or equivalent authorizing instrument
outputs: Project record with identity, category and initial justification
preconditions: A sponsoring authority has issued a charter-equivalent instrument
effects: Sponsor and project manager authority are bound to the project record

functions.name: Baseline undertaking
functions.description: Establish or amend cost, schedule and content baselines, Management Agreement or equivalent, and WBS/OBS/IMS integration ready for control.
inputs: WBS, Organizational Breakdown Structure and Integrated Master Schedule
outputs: Management Agreement or equivalent control parameters
preconditions: The project is authorized and its WBS exists
effects: The undertaking is ready for control against baselines

functions.name: Commit resources
functions.description: Bind allocations of people, funds or assets from a resource owner to WBS elements for a stated period.
outputs: Allocation records bound to WBS elements for a stated period
preconditions: A resource-owning party has committed the resource
effects: People, funds or assets are committed to the project while ownership stays with the providing party

functions.name: Report progress
functions.description: Produce the agreed periodic account of accomplishments, measures, forecast and concerns for sponsor or oversight consumers.
inputs: Accomplishments, measures, forecast and concerns for the reporting period
outputs: Periodic progress account at the agreed cadence
preconditions: A reporting cadence, audience and product are agreed
effects: Sponsor or oversight consumers receive the agreed periodic account

functions.name: Control change
functions.description: Register a proposed change, assess impact on baselines and benefits, decide, and put effectivity into force.
outputs: Change decision with impact assessment and effectivity
preconditions: The deciding authority for this class of change is identified
effects: Approved change effectivity is put into force against baselines and benefits

functions.name: Raise risk or issue
functions.description: Log an uncertain threat or opportunity or a realized issue, assign ownership and response, and escalate exceptions beyond tolerance.
inputs: Identified threat, opportunity or realized issue
outputs: Register entry with owner and response
effects: Exceptions beyond tolerance are escalated without deleting the project-level record

functions.name: Decide gate
functions.description: Assess maturity at a lifecycle review or stage boundary and record a proceed, conditional, recycle or stop decision.
inputs: Review materials and independent assurance findings
outputs: Recorded proceed, proceed-with-actions, recycle, stop or defer decision
preconditions: A Decision Authority or governing board is empowered for this gate
effects: Progression to the next phase or stage is authorized, conditioned or refused

functions.name: Transition lifecycle
functions.description: Record chartering, phase entry, suspend, resume, split, merge, abort, sponsor transfer or continuing-operations redefinition.
outputs: Typed lifecycle event with event time
preconditions: The transition is supported by a recorded decision
effects: The project's phase and operating status reflect the transition without changing identity

functions.name: Close and evaluate
functions.description: Close with a disposition, hand over or dispose of the solution, retain residual obligations, and capture post-project evaluation.
outputs: Closeout record with disposition, handover or disposal and post-project evaluation
preconditions: Blocking open items are resolved or explicitly carried as residual obligations
effects: Residual obligations and the project record survive operational close

functions.name: Tailor method and exchange record
functions.description: Record the method profile and tailoring, and export or import a projection under a named interchange profile without claiming unearned conformance.
inputs: Adopted method profile and tailoring decisions
outputs: Recorded method profile, tailoring and waivers
Exported or imported projection under the named profile
preconditions: Tailoring is approved by the requirement owner or authorized approver
effects: Alignment is recorded without being upgraded to a conformance claim
Mapping losses of the exchange are declared

composition.purpose: A programme or portfolio may contain this project as a directed investment. NASA programmes initiate and direct projects; ISO 21500/21503/21504 distinguish programme and portfolio from project; GovS 002 covers all three. A project may also stand alone.
The project decomposes work through a WBS and contains or binds assignable tasks. Tasks are not WBS identity; avoid dual masters for the same leaf work.
The project is measured through milestones and produces deliverables. Those objects keep their own schema; the project stores links, due gates, acceptance and contribution to objectives.
Sponsoring organization, performing Centers or units, contributing parties and partner agencies. Role occupancy references organization records; it does not copy them.
People occupying sponsor, manager, board, assurance and allocated-labour roles. PROV Person is an alignment for agents, not a substitute people model.

The project's intended steps, integrated master schedule and time-phased plan live in the plan model. PROV Plan is the closest open alignment: an entity representing intended actions. The project binds to a plan; it is not the plan.
Performed work that executes work packages is recorded as acts. PROV Activity is the alignment for occurrences over time that use and generate entities.
Repeatable procedures used inside the unique undertaking. PMI contrasts temporary unique projects with continuous processes; do not store process definitions here.
Align attribution, association, generation, start/end times, location and plan-used-by-agent. Do not equate Project with prov:Activity or prov:Plan.

Align context (21500), project practices (21502), WBS (21511), governance (21505) and EVM (21508). ISO 21503/21504 remain programme/portfolio siblings. Full-text clauses are paywalled; alignment is not conformance.
Align principles (justification, stages, exception, roles, products, tailoring, learning), practices and close process. PeopleCert materials do not replace ISO or NASA requirements.
Align the temporary unique endeavor definition and lifecycle-of-phases language. Do not import the full PMBOK process-group or performance-domain stack as mandatory structure.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names the master register that mints project_master_id, or assigns a UUID or ULID itself when no master or global identifier exists.
The owner package declares the adopted method profile and tailoring decisions, and never upgrades alignment with ISO, PMI, PRINCE2, NASA or GovS 002 into a conformance claim.
The owner package ships AGENTS.md carrying Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL for agent consumers.
The owner package binds a retention schedule, legal-hold register and tombstone policy before any deletion or redaction is permitted.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Namespace project identifiers under the issuing master register; where no master identifier exists the adopting Dimension assigns a UUID or ULID in its own namespace. Alternate names, codes, contract names and partner names are aliases and never the namespace key, and projection names (JSON, YAML, Git, MCP, MongoDB) are not part of the namespace.
registry_links: WM-ACT-006 — task, contained assignable work unit
WM-ACT-029 — programme or portfolio, containing investment
WM-ACT-031 — milestone and deliverable, contained delivery objects

canonicalization_rules: All time values canonicalize to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z.
Event time is stored separately from observation or ingestion time whenever those differ; planned times are labelled as planned, not as events.

Identity canonicalizes to the authoritative master-system identifier, then a governed global identifier or IRI, then a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID; dates, status values and version timestamps are never identifiers.
patch_rules: Charter, baseline, gate Decision Memorandum, allocation change and close events are append-only; corrections are new superseding events, not silent rewrites.
Baselines are replaced by creating a new baseline version and repointing current-baseline identifiers, only through recorded change control or a signed gate decision.
Authorized deletion emits a tombstone retaining project_master_id, and redaction records the authority while keeping provenance of the redaction.
compatibility_rules: Alignment with ISO, PMI, PRINCE2, NASA or GovS 002 is never silently upgraded to a conformance claim; conformance must be evidenced.
Store a named lifecycle_model rather than a single universal phase enum, so competing PMI, PRINCE2, NASA and ISO framings remain exchangeable.
Format is a projection: JSON, YAML, XML, PDF, MCP or MongoDB serializations must not be treated as the semantics of the project.
EVM fields cannot be required of every project, because some regimes mandate EVM and others explicitly do not require it.

identity_priority: UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Record event time (when the project event actually occurred: authorized, baselined, gated, closed) separately from observation or ingestion time whenever those differ. Planned times are labelled as planned, not as events.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named by project master identifier plus artifact type plus the series key: the reporting period for status reports and the gate or KDP identifier for gate or Decision Memorandum packs. Series keys never replace project_master_id as identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Charter, baseline, gate Decision Memorandum, allocation change and close events are append-only. Corrections are new events that supersede; they do not silently rewrite history. Payloads may be hashed; tombstones keep identity after authorized deletion.

policies: A project record is created only from an authorizing instrument; informal task lists do not mint a project.
Baselines and Management Agreement parameters change only through recorded change control or a signed gate decision.
Need-to-know is the default; contributing parties see their allocations, not necessarily the full charter or classified annexes.
Method tailoring is explicit. Alignment with ISO, PMI, PRINCE2, NASA or GovS 002 is never silently upgraded to a conformance claim.
Event time and ingestion time are both stored when they differ, including for delayed status ingest from scheduling tools.

read: Return identity, status, current phase, sponsor and next gate without work-package detail for portfolio consumers.
Return charter, objectives, scope and structure to authorized charter-access consumers.
Return progress, top risks and forecast to sponsor-report consumers at the agreed cadence.
Return an interchange projection under a named profile without implying that the projection is the semantics.
create: Mint a project from a charter, FAD or equivalent, assigning master identifier or Dimension ULID.
Register allocations, risks, issues, change requests and lifecycle events as new objects with event time.
Attach WBS, compliance matrix and governance map artifacts.
update: Amend justification, role occupancy, tailoring and forecasts in place only where they are current-state fields, and emit an event.
Replace baselines by creating a new baseline version and pointing current-baseline identifiers at it.
Revoke or replace access grants with expiry.
delete: Never physically destroy identity; on authorized deletion emit a tombstone retaining project_master_id.
Redact classified or personal payload under a recorded authority while keeping provenance of the redaction.
Block deletion while legal hold or residual obligation is active.

roles.name: Sponsor or Senior Responsible Owner
responsibilities: Own the business or mission outcome at senior level.
Appoint or accept the project manager and Decision Authority path.

roles.name: Project manager
responsibilities: Direct the undertaking within the Management Agreement.
Keep WBS, baselines, risks and status current.

roles.name: Decision Authority or project board
responsibilities: Decide gates, KDPs or stage boundaries.
Accept cost, schedule and content commitments.
Approve tailoring that exceeds the manager's authority.

roles.name: Resource owner
responsibilities: Commit and withdraw people, funds or assets.
Own allocation data quality for their resources.

roles.name: Assurance reviewer
responsibilities: Independently assess maturity, risk and compliance.
Record findings that the board must close or accept.

roles.name: Record steward
responsibilities: Maintain identity integrity, access grants, retention and interchange profiles.
Ensure AGENTS.md is present and current for agent consumers.

access.default_rule: Deny by default. The record owner grants least-privilege, time-bounded access. Portfolio summaries are still scoped; they are not public by default.
exceptions: Statutory audit and inspector-general access to the full file.
Classified or compartmented annexes visible only to cleared principals.
Partner-shared subsets defined by agreement, excluding unshared financial or personnel data.
Lawful whistleblowing or safety-reporting channels that bypass the project manager.
audit_requirements: Log reads of charter, baseline and gate artifacts with principal, scope, event time and ingestion time.
Log mutations to identity, justification, baselines, allocations and close disposition.
Retain audit records at least as long as the project file retention schedule.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md first to obtain Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL.

Follow Specification URL for the project meta-model, then Storage type URL for the projection in use, then Interface URL for query or MCP access, then Processes URL for authorize, baseline, report, gate and close operations.
Do not infer semantics from file extension, database collection name or Git layout.

coverage.claim: This structure is a defensible wide-union of the live primary sources retrieved for a format-neutral Project object: ISO 21500/21502/21511/21505 concepts, NASA NPR 7120.5F operating rules, UK GovS 002, PMI's public definition, PRINCE2 Version 7 method shape and W3C PROV attribution. It is not a complete ontology of all project-like work, not a substitute for paywalled full texts, and not a conformance certificate.

checklist.notes: Master register identifier, optional IRI, Dimension ULID; NASA MdM listing; dates excluded as identifiers.
ISO 21502 phases, NASA Formulation/Implementation and KDPs, PRINCE2 processes, plus suspend, abort, merge, transfer, recycle and continuing-operations variants.
Contained-by programme, contains tasks and milestones/deliverables, references organization, person, plan, act, process; peer interfaces.
RFC 3339 event versus ingestion times for authorization, allocations, gates, progress and close; planned versus actual.
PROV attribution, association, plan-used, software ingest agents; signed Decision Memoranda.
Sponsoring organization owns the record; SRO/sponsor accountability; resource owners own allocations; benefit realization may sit outside the project.
Compliance matrix, gate criteria, EVM surveillance, independent review findings; conformance claims must be evidenced.
Need-to-know default at bundle, layer, finding and artifact scopes; classified, partner, audit and safety exceptions.
Post-close archive, legal hold, tombstones, residual obligations; NASA data archival and GovS 002 disposal clauses.
Named alignments to ISO series, PMI definition, PRINCE2 7, NASA templates and PROV; projections are not semantics.
Performing Center or multi-site assignment; PROV atLocation; international partner sites.
Risk, opportunity, issue, tolerance and exception escalation.
Intended benefits and success criteria with possible programme or operations ownership after handover.

known_omissions: ISO 21502, 21500, 21511 and 21505 full texts are paywalled; clause-level field lists are inferred from abstracts, TOC fragments, ISO news and first-party summaries, not from the purchased standards.
ISO 21506:2024 vocabulary, ISO 21508:2026 EVM, ISO 21512:2024 EVM implementation guidance and ISO 21513:2026 post-project evaluation were not fetched; they are emerging or adjacent alignments.
ISO/DIS 21520 AI concepts and ISO/WD 21514 requirements and 21515 competency are under development and excluded.
PMI page HTTP fetch was blocked; the official definition is taken from the live PMI URL via search. PMBOK Guide 7 performance domains were not used as a primary schema.
UK GovS 002 full PDF and The Teal Book v3 (including a reported programme and project data standard) were not retrieved; landing-page and search descriptions were used.
DIN 69901, IPMA ICB, FIDIC/CSI construction structures, BIM information models, GAO cost-estimating guides and MS Project/PMXML schemas were not retrieved.
Legal-entity joint-venture project companies, multi-currency treasury, sanctions screening, indigenous consultation and classified compartment rules lack primary support here and remain gaps.
conflicts: PMI temporary-endeavor language conflicts with NASA continuing-operations projects that have an unspecified Phase E end and use initial capability cost. Record the variant; do not force an end date.
ISO 21500:2012 guidance on project management is withdrawn; 21500:2021 is context and 21502:2020 is project guidance. Consumers still citing 21500:2012 as the project-management standard are stale.
PMI lifecycle phase names, PRINCE2 processes, NASA A–F and ISO 21502 delivery-approach-neutral phases are competing framings. Store a named lifecycle_model rather than a single universal phase enum.
Work-package versus WM-ACT-006 task, and milestone/deliverable versus WM-ACT-031, can double-master the same object if containment is implemented as copy instead of typed link.
ISO 21502 includes benefits inside project practice; many programme methods place benefit realization above the project. Model contribution here and realization owner as a reference.
EVM is mandatory in some NASA and contract regimes and explicitly not required for other work types; it cannot be a required field of every project.
regional_assumptions: NASA NPR 7120.5F is mandatory for NASA space-flight projects and is used here as a high-rigour operating profile, not as a global law.
GovS 002 and SRO accountability apply to UK government departments and arm's length bodies; other public sectors differ.
PRINCE2 Version 7 is widely used in UK and Commonwealth public delivery; PMI vocabulary is more common in US private-sector practice.
EIA-748 EVM and US federal certification thresholds are jurisdiction-specific.
Records retention, classified markings and personal-data rules are jurisdiction-specific and only sketched.
adversarial_checks: If a consumer treats a Git repo, Mongo collection or MCP tool list as the project, they have collapsed projection into semantics; AGENTS.md and the identity priority forbid that.
If a date, gate name or version timestamp is used as the primary key, the identity priority rule is violated.

If agile product-mode work is ingested as a never-ending project without an authorizing instrument, PMI uniqueness/temporariness and ISO 21502 authorization context are violated unless a bounded undertaking is declared.
If programme, plan, process and project are stored as one object, NASA 2.1.1.1, ISO 21502's exclusion of programme/portfolio guidance and PMI project-versus-process contrast are all violated.
If baseline numbers are edited in place without a change event, NASA Management Agreement and ISO change-control practice are violated and earned-value meaning collapses.
